verdict.rationale: GoDaddy's docs confirm Bearer-token auth via Personal Access Tokens (PATs) 'tied to specific capability scopes' and show per-endpoint scope requirements (e.g. commerce.order:*, commerce.channel:read), which is the mechanism for least-privilege credentials. However, there's no dedicated guidance on creating a narrowly-scoped PAT specifically for an autonomous agent's use (the CLI agent-skill and MCP flows instead rely on the user's own full authenticated session or require no credential at all), so agent-specific scoping isn't demonstrated end-to-end. Missing for 10: explicit agent-oriented scoped-token issuance flow, a documented list/UI of selectable scopes for PAT creation, and evidence that agents are meant to use narrower PATs rather than the user's full-access session.
